summary: The required decimal string has exactly n characters, imposing an output-size lower bound of Omega(n), while the divisor is fixed to at most nine and the accepted remainder DP performs constant bounded work per output position.

optimality.argument: Any solution must materialize all n digits of the returned palindrome. The accepted construction processes each independent digit with at most nine remainders and ten digit choices, which are fixed constants under k <= 9, then mirrors O(n) characters.

replacement_checks.evidence: Returning an explicit n-digit decimal string requires writing n output characters.
Power generation, bounded-remainder suffix DP, greedy reconstruction, and mirroring each perform O(n) work because k is at most nine.

Regression evidence exhausts small lengths and all legal divisors against descending palindrome search, then validates palindrome, divisibility, length, and leading-digit properties at large and maximum lengths.
